name: Lapita Voyagers
place: the islands of the western Pacific, from New Guinea to Samoa
desc: Seafarers who sailed outrigger canoes beyond sight of land and were the first people to reach the remote islands of the Pacific, carrying pigs, dogs, chickens, taro and breadfruit, and pottery stamped with faces in fine dotted patterns. They were the ancestors of the Polynesians.
source: The Lapita type site in New Caledonia (excavated 1952); the Teouma cemetery in Vanuatu (from 2004); obsidian traced to Talasea, New Britain

cautious: felt the swell from an island beyond the horizon through the hull
belligerent: paddled three days and nights without sleep to reach a new island
devout: carried the grandmother's skull to the new island in a pot

inventions.name: Outrigger Canoe
inventions.source: Austronesian outrigger and double-hulled canoes carried the Lapita people thousands of kilometres across open ocean
inventions.desc: A hull with a float on a boom beside it, so it cannot capsize in the ocean swell: fishing yields 25% more, everyone carries 1 more.
inventions.hint: Needs Polished Stone Tools, and builders who fish.

inventions.name: Wayfinding
inventions.source: Pacific navigators steered by the rising and setting points of stars, the swells, the birds and the clouds, without instruments
inventions.desc: Knowing where each star rises and sets, and reading the swells and the birds: people see much farther and travel 4% faster.
inventions.hint: Comes from long scouting, and from watching the sky.

inventions.name: Dentate-Stamped Pottery
inventions.source: Lapita pots were decorated with tiny comb-like stamps pressed into the clay, making stylised human faces and patterns
inventions.desc: Pots pricked with tiny toothed stamps into faces with long eyes: +2 mood, rites bring 5% more devotion.

inventions.name: Giant Clam Adze
inventions.source: On islands without good stone, adzes were ground from the thick shell of the giant clam
inventions.desc: A heavy blade ground from the shell of the giant clam, for hollowing canoes: woodcutting 12% faster.

foods.name: Taro Pudding
foods.desc: Taro roots baked in an earth oven and pounded with coconut cream: hunger grows 10% slower.

foods.name: Fermented Breadfruit
foods.source: Pacific islanders stored breadfruit for years by fermenting it in leaf-lined pits
foods.desc: Breadfruit buried in leaf-lined pits to ferment, food for voyages and for the lean season: food spoils 15% slower.

finds.name: Wild Taro
finds.desc: Big-leaved plants of the wet ground with starchy roots.

finds.name: Breadfruit Trees
finds.desc: Tall trees with big round fruit that tastes like bread when roasted.

people.name: Hokule
people.desc: She knows a hundred stars and the island under each of them.
memory: found an island by watching which way the boobies flew at dusk

people.name: Waka
people.desc: He can hollow a canoe from a single tree in a moon.
memory: lashed the outrigger to the first canoe that reached this island

people.name: The Ancestors of Teouma
people.source: The Teouma cemetery, Efate, Vanuatu, c. 1000 BCE; many skulls had been removed and kept, and some placed in pots
people.desc: The first settlers of Vanuatu, whose skulls their children took up after burial and kept, some in decorated pots, as treasured ancestors.

people.name: The Potters of Site 13
people.source: Site WKO013A at Lapita, New Caledonia, which gave its name to the whole culture
people.desc: The women and men whose stamped pots, found on a beach in New Caledonia, gave a name to the first settlers of the remote Pacific.

people.name: Talasea
people.source: Obsidian from Talasea on New Britain travelled some 4,500 km, as far as Fiji
people.text: a paddler from the big island in the west, with a bag of black glass from the fire mountain, looking for new islands to trade with.
memory: paddled from the fire mountain to an island no one had named
people.desc: An obsidian trader named after the source of his stone.

people.name: Maui
people.label: Maui, Fisher of Islands
people.desc: The trickster who pulls islands from the sea with his hook. Foraging 8, Lore 6.

people.name: Tupaia
people.label: Tupaia the Navigator
people.desc: A much later heir of the Lapita voyagers, who drew 74 islands from memory for Captain Cook in 1769. Lore 8, Foraging 6.

people.name: Hiro
people.label: Hiro, Builder of the Great Canoe
people.desc: He builds the double canoe that crosses the ocean. Crafting 8.

events.title: Beyond the Horizon
events.source: Lapita people crossed the 850 km of open sea from the Solomons to Vanuatu and Fiji, sailing against the prevailing winds so they could always return
events.text: The navigators have seen birds flying out to sea each morning and returning each evening. There is land beyond the horizon. Shall we load a canoe with pigs, taro and seed, and go?

options.label: Sail into the wind

do.feat: Found an island beyond the horizon

options.result: After nine days a green line rises from the sea. The canoes come home to tell, and some stay to plant.

options.label: Stay on our island
options.result: The birds keep flying out each morning. Someday.

events.title: Keeping the Ancestors
events.text: A respected elder has been buried for a season. As the old custom goes, the family wants to take up the skull and keep it in a stamped pot, so the elder can travel with them to any new island.

events.title: The Great Wind
events.text: A cyclone has torn through the island, flattening the gardens and breaking canoes on the reef.

options.label: Rebuild the canoes first
options.result: With the canoes repaired, the sea feeds everyone while the gardens regrow.

options.label: Dig the breadfruit pits
options.result: The stored breadfruit, sour and strong, carries everyone through.

tales.name: Maui Fishes Up the Islands
tales.source: Polynesian tradition, told from New Zealand to Hawaii
tales.text: Maui made a fish-hook from his grandmother's jawbone and went fishing with his brothers. Far out at sea his hook caught on something enormous. He hauled and hauled, and up out of the sea came an island, then another and another, with the canoes' wake still on their hills.
tales.moral: the sea gives land to the bold

tales.name: The House of the Stars
tales.source: The Pacific star compass, kept in memory by navigators
tales.text: Around the canoe is a great round house with many doors. Each star comes out of its own door in the east and goes in at its own door in the west. Learn the doors, and you will never be lost; the island you seek always lies under one of them.
tales.moral: know the stars and you are never lost

tales.name: The Three Who Came in the Canoe
tales.source: A story made up around the animals the Lapita carried
tales.text: When the first canoe came to the empty island, three passengers argued about who was most useful. Pig said: I am food for the feast. Dog said: I guard the house. Chicken said: I wake you for the voyage. The navigator said: that is why all three of you came.

tales.name: The Landfall Feast
tales.source: A story made up around the settling of new islands
tales.text: Each year on the day the first canoe reached this island, the people make an earth oven on the beach, roast pig and taro, and the oldest navigator names every island between here and home, one by one, until the fire burns low.
